THOUGHT: The patient is an older adult with progressive fatigue, pallor, petechiae, and splenomegaly—signs of marrow dysfunction and bleeding tendency. CBC shows severe anemia (Hgb 8.3 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (platelets 35,600/mm3), and marked leukocytosis (WBC 81,000/mm3) with immature cells on smear. The peripheral smear description—immature cells with large prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions—is characteristic of myeloblasts containing Auer rods. These findings are most consistent with an acute myeloid leukemia (blasts predominating and causing marrow failure), and the presence of numerous Auer rods is particularly suggestive of the promyelocytic subtype (acute promyelocytic leukemia, APL). Confirmation requires urgent bone marrow biopsy with flow cytometry and cytogenetics (look for t(15;17) in APL), and APL in particular is a hematologic emergency because of high risk of coagulopathy (DIC).

DIAGNOSIS: Acute myeloid leukemia — most consistent with acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL).
